item.content:encoded: The article was great, but I particularly liked the comment at the end which referenced the statue of David and how there may or may not be a Goliath statue dead set on snapping it in two.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
What about just changing the title? The year isn't mentioned in the article until the reader is several paragraphs in, but in the title it's the first thing they see. Maybe something like "Untitled Jewelry Piece (Clarice's Doom), Circa Late 15th Century".

On the top rated new pages page, the number caught my eye before even the words and I went into it with my first impression being one of worry that the story would be one big dog whistle. It wasn't until the mention of Lorenzo de Medici that I realized she was a real person and I googled her to find her death date.

I'm a total sucker for the "fantasy explanation for real event in history" trope, so I want this tale to do well.

item.title: Ciao Bella Author Commentary Something or Other
item.content:encoded:
Yeah I can't think of a Commentary Pun. Sue me.

This a GOI Format for the Italian branch GOI "The Medicean Academy of Occult Arts", an organization which deals with pre- and early-modern anart, particularly from the Renaissance era. It's been a blast to write for this so far, and we're hoping that the rest of the works are going to be just as good.

I'm aware that this looks like a garbage fire on mobile. We're going to try to rectify that. Clusterfuck Rectified! Hopefully!

Marten head: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Italian_-_Marten%27s_Head_-_Walters_571982_-_View_B.jpg In the public domain in its country of Origin.

Medici Logo: Created by TSATPWTCOTTTADC.

Also, I'm aware of the implications of the number. It's the year Clarice Orsini died. Unless I can build a time machine that allows me to kill her a year earlier, there's not much I can do about it.
